At SpaceXSI we are building the high-performance inference platform that serves Grok to millions of users every day.
As a Software Engineer, Training/Inference (C++), you will design and optimize large-scale model serving systems end-to-end.

NETWORK ENGINEER, HIGH-SPEED INTERCONNECTS (ML INFRASTRUCTURE)
SpaceXSI is building at a furious pace with the latest compute and switching hardware to help people understand the universe.

This strategic role will drive innovation in high-bandwidth, low-latency, power-efficient interconnects critical for AI/ML clusters based on advanced computing platforms.

Engineers will own all aspects from design and development to build and operations.

You will focus on the physical layer and system-level integration of copper (ACC, AEC, CPC) and optical (FRO, LRO/TRO, LPO, AOC, CPO) interconnects that directly determine the performance, power efficiency, scale, and cost of next-generation AI/ML clusters.
This is a highly technical, hands-on role bridging ML cluster requirements with cutting-edge interconnect hardware - ideal for engineers who love both large-scale AI systems and the physics/engineering of 200G+ SerDes, PAM4, photonics, signal integrity and diagnostics.

Collaborate with ML training teams to translate workload communication patterns into concrete interconnect topology and optical reconfigurability requirements

Ensure compliance with relevant standards (NERC, ERCOT, IEEE, NEC, NFPA, UL) and support permitting and utility coordination
Support equipment specification, vendor selection, factory testing, site commissioning, and energization

Background with data centers, hyperscale facilities, or large on-site power infrastructure (>50 MW)
Knowledge of ERCOT, NERC reliability standards, and utility interconnection processes

section_intro:
SECURITY ENGINEER, GRC SALES
We are seeking a Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) professional focused on third-party risk management and customer trust.
This role sits at the intersection of cybersecurity GRC, vendor management, and sales enablement: you will act as a security-minded presales engineer for the sales team, develop enough depth in the SpaceXSI technical environment to accurately complete customer vendor security questionnaires, join customer meetings as the security and compliance subject matter expert, and help operate third-party risk and vendor management processes.
The ideal candidate brings a cybersecurity and GRC perspective - fluent in how AI LLMs, CI/CD pipelines, identity and access management, DevOps, DevSecOps, Kubernetes, and IT/AI governance actually work in production - and can translate that understanding into clear, credible answers for enterprise buyers without slowing deals or overstating our posture.
This role may also include additional tasks and responsibilities as needed to support the team and evolving business priorities.
section_responsibilities:
Support the sales organization as a cybersecurity/GRC presales partner: attend customer and prospect meetings, present our security and compliance posture, and answer technical and control-related questions with accuracy and judgment
Own and continuously improve responses to customer vendor security questionnaires, RFPs, SIG/CAIQ-style assessments, and due-diligence requests; maintain a reusable knowledge base of control narratives grounded in how SpaceXSI actually operates
Build and maintain working fluency across the SpaceXSI environment - AI/LLM systems and model governance, CI/CD pipelines, identity and access management, DevOps and DevSecOps practices, Kubernetes platforms, and governance of IT and AI environments - sufficient to answer customer questions and escalate appropriately to engineering when needed
Partner with Engineering, Security, Legal, and Product to keep questionnaire content, Trust Center materials, and security collateral current as architecture, controls, and certifications evolve
Translate customer security requirements into actionable internal asks; help distinguish must-have contractual or control commitments from unreasonable or out-of-scope demands
Contribute to policies, standards, and procedures related to third-party risk, customer assurance, and vendor security due diligence
Coordinate with the broader GRC and security teams on overlapping frameworks and evidence (e.g., SOC 2, ISO 27001, ISO 42001, privacy commitments) so external answers remain consistent with our internal control environment and GRC tooling (e.g., Vanta)
Identify patterns in customer questionnaires and deal blockers; feed those insights back into product, engineering, and GRC roadmaps to reduce friction over time
Create and present concise status updates on questionnaire volume, deal-impacting security asks, vendor risk posture, and emerging customer assurance themes to sales leadership and GRC stakeholders
Champion clear, honest customer communication - building trust by explaining what we do, how we govern AI and infrastructure, and where we are intentionally scoping risk

3+ years of experience in cybersecurity, GRC, third-party risk management, security assurance, or a role with customer-facing or sales-adjacent responsibilities
PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:
Demonstrated experience completing or owning customer vendor security questionnaires and participating in security due-diligence discussions with enterprise buyers
Working technical fluency across several of the following: AI/LLM or ML platforms, CI/CD pipelines, identity and access management, DevOps/DevSecOps, Kubernetes, and cloud environments (AWS, GCP, or Azure) - enough to understand control implications and speak credibly with engineers and customers

5+ years of cybersecurity, GRC, third-party risk, or customer trust / security assurance experience (mid-to-senior scope)
Prior experience in a presales security, solutions engineering (security), customer trust, or sales-enablement GRC role at a technology, cloud, or AI company

Familiarity with AI governance topics relevant to customer diligence (e.g., model data handling, prompt/output controls, training-data boundaries, ISO 42001 / NIST AI RMF concepts, EU AI Act awareness)
Experience maintaining a Trust Center, security FAQ library, or questionnaire knowledge base; familiarity with GRC platforms such as Vanta, Drata, or similar
Ability to read architecture diagrams, IAM models, and pipeline/Kubernetes high-level designs and turn them into accurate, non-jargon customer narratives
Comfort operating in fast-moving deal cycles while protecting accuracy - knowing when to say "I'll confirm with engineering" versus answering from established evidence
Working knowledge of data privacy frameworks (e.g., GDPR, CCPA) as they appear in enterprise security and vendor assessments
Certifications such as CISSP, CISA, CISM, CRISC, CTPRP, CIPT, CIPP/US, or similar preferred
Experience supporting public sector, financial services, or other highly regulated customer diligence processes

section_intro:
HEAD OF FINANCIAL CRIME
The UK financial crime program is being built now, and it has to stand up to the FCA.
This role sits in Compliance, reports to the US BSA/AML Officer, and owns the UK framework end to end - AML/CTF, sanctions, fraud, ABC, KYC/CDD/EDD, transaction monitoring, SARs, and the operating rhythm.
You will still work the hard cases.
It is a builder seat with accountability, not a queue job with "strategy" in the title.
If you have eight or more years inside an FCA-regulated bank, EMI, PI, or payments firm, have owned or rebuilt a financial crime control framework, and can still open a file, this is the seat.
You will build the UK program from the ground up, setting the standards the team and the FCA will use.
This is consumer-scale payments financial crime work - not a private-banking book - and you'll sit directly with Product and Engineering.
You'll operate in a small team with a direct line to the US BSA/AML Officer, where scope is broad and process is lean.
The measure of success is a program that still works a year later, and the role sits alongside MLRO / SMF17-adjacent duties for the UK entity.
section_responsibilities:
Design and run the UK financial crime programme: policy, procedures, CDD/EDD, risk rating, sanctions screening, transaction monitoring, SAR handling, escalation, QA, and training
Turn MLR 2017, POCA, the Sanctions and Anti-Money Laundering Act, JMLSG, the FCA Financial Crime Guide, SYSC 6.3, and payments/EMI expectations into something operations and product can run
Own the UK business-wide risk assessment and keep it honest as the product, customer mix, and channels change
Handle complex cases - PEPs, adverse media, sanctions hits, high-risk onboarding, fraud typologies, escalations - then use the queue to fix the framework
Stand up first- and second-line controls: documentation, workflows, vendor oversight, quality sampling, MI, and issue management
Put UK requirements into the customer journey with Legal, Operations, Product, and Engineering.
Be the UK voice in global design decisions
Report on quality, residual risk, throughput, and control health, and prepare the program for internal audit, skilled-person reviews, and FCA scrutiny
Build the operating model as the team grows.
Hire, coach, and set the standard
Support MLRO / SMF17-adjacent duties as the UK permissions model requires

section_intro: Mechanical Commissioning Technician
section_about:
We are seeking a highly skilled Mechanical Commissioning Technician to support the buildout and startup of SpaceXAI's high-performance data centers.
In this critical hands-on role, you will perform commissioning, testing, and troubleshooting of mechanical systems that cool and support our next-generation AI supercomputing infrastructure.
You will work closely with construction, engineering, and operations teams to ensure safe, reliable, and high-quality mechanical systems from initial installation through full system turnover.
This is a full-time, onsite role with significant travel to SpaceXAI data center sites.
section_responsibilities:
Execute mechanical commissioning activities for chilled water, condenser water, cooling towers, pumps, heat exchangers, air handlers, computer-room cooling, liquid-cooling equipment, and associated controls in data center environments.
Perform flush, fill, leak, and pressure tests; verify valve lineup, flow, temperature, and pressure against design and sequence of operations.
Complete point-to-point checks with controls technicians and confirm sensors, actuators, interlocks, and alarms respond correctly.
Troubleshoot and resolve mechanical issues during pre-commissioning, commissioning, and startup phases.
Develop and execute detailed commissioning test procedures, scripts, and documentation in accordance with project specifications and industry standards.
Collaborate with EPC contractors, OEM vendors, and SpaceXAI engineers to coordinate startup sequences and integrated system testing.
Walk systems against drawings, mark redlines, write punch-list items, and drive closeout until deficiencies are cleared.
Ensure strict adherence to safety protocols, LOTO procedures, and quality standards during all commissioning activities.
Maintain accurate as-built documentation, test records, and commissioning reports.
Support training of operations and maintenance teams on commissioned mechanical systems.
Participate in constructability reviews and provide field feedback to improve design and installation quality.
section_requirements:
3+ years of hands-on mechanical, HVAC, pipefitting, or commissioning experience in data centers, power plants, or large industrial facilities.
Strong working knowledge of chilled-water plants, pumping systems, heat transfer equipment, and related mechanical distribution.
Experience with commissioning and field test equipment (pressure gauges, flow meters, temperature instruments, leak-detection tools, etc.).
Ability to read and interpret piping and instrumentation diagrams, mechanical drawings, and equipment submittals.
Strong safety mindset with current OSHA 10/30 or equivalent training.

Ability to travel extensively to SpaceXAI construction sites and remain onsite during peak commissioning phases.
Capability to work in industrial environments, climb ladders, lift moderate loads, and wear PPE for extended periods.

As a member of the Supercomputer Physical Infrastructure team, you will provide hands-on support for the integration, commissioning, troubleshooting, and maintenance of control systems across our AI training campuses.

NETWORK ENGINEER
SpaceXSI is building and operating large-scale networks that underpin training and inference infrastructure, including high-performance / supercompute fabrics that connect GPU clusters, plus the core, edge, and datacenter networks that keep that infrastructure reachable and reliable.
We need a Network Engineer who is strong on fundamentals and comfortable owning production network design, deployment, and operations end to end.
This is a hands-on engineering seat - not a NOC technician role and not a network-software (telemetry/ZTP platform) SWE role.
You will design and build networks, qualify platforms, ship changes safely, and keep availability and performance high as we scale.

section_responsibilities:
Design, deploy, and operate production datacenter and campus/core networks at scale
Own routing and switching configuration standards (BGP and at least one IGP such as OSPF or IS-IS), including change design, peer reviews, and execution
Qualify new network platforms, optics, and topologies; contribute to architecture and capacity planning
Build and improve monitoring, alerting, and operational documentation so issues are caught and fixed quickly
Troubleshoot Layer 2/Layer 3 incidents end to end - from link flaps and optics through routing and traffic engineering - and drive root cause and lasting fixes
Automate repetitive network tasks with Python, Ansible, or similar tooling where it reduces toil
Partner with compute, facilities, and software teams during cluster build-outs and maintenance windows
Support high-performance / supercompute network environments (Ethernet AI/HPC fabrics, RoCE/RDMA-capable designs) as part of the broader network estate

5+ years of experience designing and/or operating production networks in a datacenter, ISP, cloud, or large enterprise environment
PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:
Experience troubleshooting live production network incidents and participating in on-call
Experience with BGP and at least one interior routing protocol
Strong written and verbal communication; clear change docs and incident notes
Working knowledge of TCP/IP, VLANs, EVPN/VXLAN or equivalent datacenter overlays, and optics / high-speed Ethernet
Experience with modern datacenter vendors (e.g.
Arista, Cisco, Juniper, Nvidia/Mellanox)
Familiarity with high-performance or supercompute networking (RoCEv2, congestion control, GPU cluster fabrics) - useful context for our environment, not a hard filter
Network automation (Python, Ansible, Terraform, or similar) used in production
Experience with EVPN, leaf-spine, and large-scale Ethernet fabrics
Prior work supporting rapid datacenter or cluster capacity build-outs
Deep specialist RoCE/NCCL ownership is a plus, not the bar for this seat

Willing to work onsite in Palo Alto

section_intro:
CONSTRUCTION SCHEDULER
Develop, maintain, and communicate construction schedules that the field, subcontractors, and leadership can actually use.
You will build CPM baselines, update them from real progress, flag risk early, and explain schedule impact of changes, delays, and recovery plans.
This is not a data-entry role.
You need enough means-and-methods knowledge to challenge a sequence that will not work in the field.
Superintendents run the work; project managers own cost and contracts; the scheduler is the person who can tell you what is actually driving the end date, what slips if a trade is late, and whether a recovery plan is real.
section_responsibilities:
Build baseline CPM schedules from drawings, specs, estimates, bid packages, and construction sequences (WBS, activity coding, logic, calendars, and constraints used sparingly and correctly)
Maintain the live schedule: collect progress from superintendents, project managers, and trades; update percent complete, remaining duration, and logic; publish a clean current-period update on a set cadence (typically weekly look-aheads and monthly official updates)
Own the critical path.
Identify near-critical work, float erosion, and out-of-sequence progress.
Tell the team why the end date moved, not just that it did
Produce three-week (or similar) look-aheads that match the master schedule and what the field can actually crew
Analyze schedule impact of RFIs, change orders, design late-outs, access constraints, long-lead procurement, weather, and labor shortages.
Prepare time-impact analyses (TIA) and what-if, recovery, and acceleration scenarios
Coordinate with project managers, superintendents, estimators, procurement, design, owners/CMs, and subcontractors so the schedule reflects committed dates, not wishful ones
Resource-load and, where required, cost-load the schedule.
Flag crew stacking, craft shortages, and unrealistic production rates
Prepare narratives, variance reports, S-curves, histograms, and executive summaries for internal reviews and owner/CM submittals
Support claims and delay documentation with contemporaneous records (as-planned vs. as-built, fragnets, delay categorization) when needed
Enforce schedule standards: naming, coding, update process, backup, and version control so the file remains auditable
Facilitate or support pull-planning / Last Planner sessions and convert those commitments into logic in the CPM model
Visit the site regularly.
A scheduler who never walks the job will be wrong

section_intro:
MANAGER, ENGINEERING (POWER GENERATION & UTILITIES)
We are looking for a Manager of Engineering to own the design, build-out, commissioning, and continuous improvement of automation, controls, and electrical systems at SpaceXSI's power generation facility in Southaven.
This plant is critical infrastructure for SpaceXSI's AI supercomputers: it must deliver high-reliability power and supporting utilities at scale, with the uptime and response expected of a mission-critical compute campus.
If it has a gas or steam turbine control system, a switchgear lineup, a plant electrical distribution network, a SCADA/DCS point, a control loop, or a supporting utility/process system (water, wastewater, fuel gas, HVAC, cooling) that must run reliably, this team designs it, specifies it, commissions it, and keeps it running.
As a Manager, you will lead a team of engineers in a high-reliability, fast-paced environment.
This is a hands-on technical leadership role - you will review P&IDs, challenge control philosophies, dive into DCS/PLC architecture, electrical protection schemes, and commissioning details, not just manage a roadmap.
You will scale both the team and the systems as generation capacity and AI compute load grow.
section_responsibilities:
Own automation, controls, and electrical scope for power generation assets (gas turbine simple cycle, combined cycle, and steam turbine systems) and plant electrical systems, including DCS/SCADA architecture, PLC systems, turbine control interfaces, switchgear, protection and metering, plant distribution, instrumentation, and control networks - from control philosophy through commissioning and reliability, in compliance with NFPA 70/70B/70E, NESC, and IEEE standards
Lead controls scope for mechanical and electrical balance-of-plant and supporting utilities, including fuel gas, HVAC, fire protection, compressed air, cooling water, raw water intake, demineralization, wastewater treatment, and industrial gas systems that keep the plant and downstream compute campus online
Build, mentor, and manage a team of automation and controls engineers and technicians; scale the team with power generation capacity growth and AI supercomputer demand
Review and approve control philosophy documents, I/O lists, control narratives, single-line diagrams, electrical/pneumatic schematics, cause-and-effect diagrams, and control panel designs; drive standardized DCS/PLC/SCADA architecture, cybersecurity posture, documentation, and engineering practices across the Southaven facilities
Interface with internal engineering, construction, OEMs (turbine, HRSG, BOP, and electrical equipment vendors), and contractors; develop SOWs, negotiate, and manage contractor work to keep controls and electrical scope integrated and on schedule
Own field commissioning for automation, controls, and electrical systems (loop checks, functional testing, protection testing, start-up, and hand-off) and drive root-cause investigations and reliability improvements on operating assets

Join the power generation engineering team to design, commission, and maintain plant control systems.

As a Supervisor on the power generation team, you will lead the technicians who operate, maintain, and repair on-site generation that powers SpaceXSI's high-density AI supercomputing facilities.
You will oversee plant technicians, process technicians, and electrical technicians as one operations and maintenance team - covering gas turbine packages, balance-of-plant, process/fluid systems, and plant electrical systems through 34.5 kV.

section_intro:
MANAGER, OPERATION & MAINTENANCE (POWER PLANT)
We are seeking a Manager of Operation & Maintenance to lead the people who keep SpaceXSI's on-site power plant running.
You will oversee supervisors, leads, and technicians supporting operations and maintenance of gas turbine generation, balance-of-plant, process and fluid systems, and plant electrical systems.
This plant supplies power for high-density AI supercomputing facilities in the Memphis and Southaven area, and it has to stay online.
This is a hands-on leadership role.
You will set the operating and maintenance standard, run the organization through trips, outages, and day-to-day work, and build supervisors and technicians who can execute safely without waiting on you for every decision.
You will work with engineering, construction, operations leadership, OEMs, and contractors as the plant grows.
This is a full-time, onsite role based in the Memphis region.

Lead supervisors, leads, and technicians across plant, process, and electrical crafts as one O&M organization

Enforce SpaceXSI safety standards, including LOTO, NFPA 70E / arc-flash, confined space, and hot work.
Stop work when conditions are unsafe and hold the organization to that standard
Lead outage planning and execution with engineering, OEMs, and contractors, and support commissioning and turnover of new generation and BOP systems into operations
Own O&M vendor and contractor performance, cost, and schedule.
Work with buyers and accounts payable so accounts and contracts stay in order
Drive reliability: bad-actor elimination, root-cause investigations, and standards that raise uptime as capacity grows
Coach and develop supervisors and leads.
Set expectations, manage performance, and scale the team with the plant
Communicate plant status, risks, team performance, and resource needs to site leadership

The plant supplies power for high-density AI supercomputing facilities in the Memphis and Southaven area, and it has to stay online 24/7.
You will work across gas turbines and generators, balance-of-plant, fuel gas and process/fluid systems, water, compressed and instrument air, HVAC and cooling, and plant electrical systems.
The turbine fleet is several different manufacturers.
You are expected to be proficient on every type on site, not specialized in one OEM.
You will troubleshoot equipment, direct contractors, and use AI to simplify how the plant is operated and maintained.
Your schedule flexes, including nights, weekends, holidays, and callouts, so the plant always has engineering coverage.
This is a full-time, on-site role in the Memphis region.

section_intro:
INSTRUMENTATION & CONTROLS TECHNICIAN (POWER GENERATION)
As an Instrumentation & Controls Technician, you will keep the controls and field instruments reliable on SpaceXSI's on-site power plant.
The plant supplies power for high-density AI supercomputing facilities in the Memphis and Southaven area, and it has to stay online 24/7.
You will calibrate, troubleshoot, and repair the instruments and controls on 40+ aeroderivative and industrial gas turbines and their generators, plus balance-of-plant, fuel gas, water, compressed and instrument air, HVAC, cooling, fire and gas, and emissions systems.
The turbines come from several manufacturers on three control platforms, and you are expected to be proficient on every type on site, not specialized in one OEM.
When a unit trips, you find out why.
The cause is usually small and physical, like a cracked sense line, a chafed thermocouple lead, or a fitting that backed off, and you fix it so it stays fixed.
Your schedule flexes, including nights, weekends, holidays, and callouts, so the plant always has I&C coverage.
This is a full-time, on-site role in the Memphis region.
section_responsibilities:
Own I&C trip response: trace the first-out and historian trends to the failed device, fix it, walk the unit down, and disposition every alarm before restart
Troubleshoot three turbine control platforms online in Studio 5000 (ControlLogix and GuardLogix, FLEX and FLEX 5000 I/O), tracing trips, permissives, and limiters to the field device
Calibrate and repair transmitters (HART), thermocouples, RTDs, analyzers, control valves, and actuators; make up tubing, fittings, and sensor leads that survive engine heat and vibration
Maintain vibration, speed, and overspeed protection (proximity probes, accelerometers, speed pickups, Dynamix 1444), and tell a sensor fault from a machine fault
Restore EtherNet/IP device-level rings, remote I/O, and the fiber and copper links between turbine controllers and the plant SCADA
Keep fire and gas detection, CO2 suppression, CEMS (daily calibrations, CGA, RATA), and SCR ammonia controls tested and in compliance
Run loop and functional checks during commissioning, start-up, and outages, and catch loose terminations, grounds, and unsupported tubing before they cause a trip
Record as-found/as-left results in the CMMS, fix repeat failures at the cause through management of change, and use AI tools to troubleshoot and document faster
Follow SpaceXSI safety procedures (LOTO, NFPA 70E / arc-flash, confined space, hot work), clear every lockout and bypass before restart, and stop work when conditions are unsafe

Gas turbine controls from more than one OEM, aeroderivative and industrial (GE LM6000 or LM2500, Solar Titan with Turbotronic)
Allen-Bradley ControlLogix and GuardLogix in Studio 5000 with FLEX and FLEX 5000 I/O; Siemens S7 (TIA Portal) is a plus

Fire and gas (Det-Tronics or similar), CEMS (NOx, CO, O2; CGA and RATA), and SCR aqueous ammonia systems
Generator protection, excitation, and synchronizing (SEL, Beckwith, Basler), including relay event retrieval and DC control power
Trip investigations, commissioning, and outages worked from historian trends (Ignition or similar SCADA), P&IDs, loop sheets, and cause-and-effect charts

Must be able to lift up to 25 lbs unassisted

Most construction managers inherit a schedule someone else built and a set of contractors someone else hired.

SpaceX builds its own launch sites, factories, test stands, and AI superclusters - and it plans to keep building.

Clear written and verbal communication, including control narratives, sequences of operations, and recommendations across mechanical, electrical, and operations teams.

Experience in data centers, power generation, district energy, industrial utilities, or other 24/7 process plants.
Experience in at least one of the disciplines below, with a real interest in learning the others.
Sizing and application of motors, VFDs, starters, valves, actuators, instrumentation, and circuit protection for pumps, fans, towers, and plant equipment.
Design of fail-safe circuits using safety relays and safety controllers, including interlocks that must hold during a loss of power or a controls failure.
Hands-on troubleshooting of industrial electrical systems with multimeters, oscilloscopes, and network diagnostics.
Reading and producing schematics, panel layouts, riser diagrams, and one-line diagrams (EPLAN preferred).
Fieldbus and Ethernet plant networks: BACnet/IP, Modbus TCP, EtherNet/IP, Profinet, and OPC UA.
Designing, building, and commissioning control panels and electromechanical systems with arc-flash, lockout/tagout, and construction-power constraints in mind.
Working knowledge of NEC, NFPA 70E, UL 508A, and data center facility standards, with the ability to apply them to control design.
PLC programming in structured text and ladder, preferably Rockwell (Studio 5000), Siemens TIA Portal, or Beckhoff TwinCAT.
HMI, BMS, and SCADA development - Ignition, Niagara, or an equivalent platform - focused on fast navigation, meaningful alarms, trends, and equipment health.
Industrial protocols used in critical facilities: BACnet/IP, Modbus TCP, OPC UA, MQTT, SNMP, EtherNet/IP, and Profinet.
Applying control software to mechanical and electrical assemblies: sensors, VFDs, valves, and pump or fan systems, including a disciplined checkout before a system is allowed to carry load.
Experience with EPMS, power metering, generator or ATS status, and historian or alarming tools used to operate a data center.
ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:
Ability to work long hours, nights, and weekends when commissioning, failover testing, or a live plant event requires it.
Willingness to work on site in the data center, including mechanical plants, electrical rooms, and the data halls, for checkout and troubleshooting.

section_intro:
GLOBAL GOVERNMENT AFFAIRS DIRECTOR
We are seeking Global Government Affairs Director to support SpaceXSI's business and growth objectives primarily in London/UK through direct global lobbying efforts and strategic coalition building on a range of issues.
You will own SpaceXSI's market development and stakeholder engagement strategy for the region.
You will lead efforts to position SpaceXSI as the trusted partner for frontier AI deployments across the European governments.
This role combines strategic market leadership, high-level stakeholder engagement, revenue acceleration, and cross-functional influence.
You will operate as an individual contributor while collaborating closely with global and local leadership to ensure government priorities align with and inform SpaceXSI's broader international growth.
section_responsibilities:
Lead the identification, qualification, and development of European governments and strategic enterprise opportunities, building and managing a robust pipeline for Enterprise Sales teams to convert into revenue-generating agreements
Conduct rigorous market research and competitive analysis to assess demand for SpaceXSI's technologies, map the European AI and public sector landscape, identify barriers to entry, and develop strategies that accelerate SpaceXSI's growth in Europe
Elevate SpaceXSI's brand and presence in Europe as a mission-driven, trusted leader in frontier AI, positioning the company as the partner of choice for transformative public sector and critical national infrastructure initiatives
Build and expand a senior-level network of advocates and partners across Europe national governments, local government, academia, industry bodies, and the private sector to champion SpaceXSI's growth and open strategic doors
Drive significant increases in win rates on complex European government and strategic enterprise deals by providing strategic counsel, executive sponsorship, and high-touch enablement to pursuit and sales teams
Shape favorable funding, procurement, policy, and regulatory conditions that enable SpaceXSI's successful market entry, expansion, and long-term positioning in Europe
Provide executive-level air cover and personal leadership on the highest-priority European pursuits, including leading government briefings, negotiations, and strategic relationship management
Accelerate deal velocity from opportunity identification through contract award, signature, and successful launch, removing obstacles and orchestrating cross-functional resources
Partner with global Sales, Engineering, Product, and Legal teams to improve competitive positioning, tailor solutions to public sector requirements, and maximize win probability on strategic opportunities
Lead cross-functional alignment with Sales, Marketing, Legal, Product, Engineering, and Finance to ensure European market strategy and execution are fully integrated with SpaceXSI's global priorities and product roadmap
Deliver high-impact enablement resources, market intelligence, and thought leadership that accelerate opportunities.
Systematically gather and synthesize European customer requirements and advocate for them with product and engineering teams to iterate and enhance SpaceXSI offerings for public sector use cases
Shape customer and stakeholder thinking of aligning with SpaceXSI's unique strengths and value proposition, helping European governments understand how frontier AI can transform their missions
Contribute to and help enable SpaceXSI's global government affairs strategy from the European vantage point, ensuring strong coordination and knowledge sharing across EMEA and other international markets
Cultivate and sustain trusted senior relationships with ministers, senior civil servants, agency leaders, regulators, and strategic partners to create durable competitive advantage
Proactively monitor, analyze, and mitigate geopolitical, economic, regulatory, policy, security, and reputational risks in the region that could affect market access, compliance, or ongoing operations; develop and execute mitigation and contingency plans
Define, track, and report on key performance metrics - including pipeline value, win rates, deals closed, policy/regulatory milestones, and revenue impact - and provide regular strategic updates to global leadership
